evals.prompt: stage: growth. We are adding one-click shareable report links to our data-report SaaS. compete.md says users mostly use Excel pivot tables and screenshots in WeChat; reviews of a rival BI tool complain that sharing needs every viewer to have a paid seat. Write the positioning and highlight hypotheses.
evals.expected_output: Derives positioning from the real alternatives (Excel + screenshots, rival BI seat-gated sharing) → unique attribute (viewer needs no account/seat) → value (weekly report reaches the boss in seconds) → best-fit segment (ops leads who report upward weekly) → frame. Compares at least two positioning options and recommends one with evidence. Highlights are ≤3 demonstrable moments tied to a journey step, each with proof and the objection it answers. Segments are behaviour-defined, with missing events listed as tracking requests. No adjective-only slogan, no launch copy.
expectations: Lists competitive alternatives including the status quo (Excel / screenshots)
Compares at least two positioning options and recommends one
Each highlight names a journey step or moment the user can see
Segments are defined by behaviour or lifecycle, not demographics only
Does NOT write final launch copy or claim the feature is already verified

rubric.criterion: Positioning is derived from the alternatives users actually use, citing the compete evidence
At least two genuinely different positioning options with a reasoned recommendation
Highlights are concrete, demonstrable moments with proof and the objection they answer
Target segments are computable from product data; data gaps become tracking requests

evals.prompt: stage: accept. The briefing claims 'export to Excel in one click' and 'report ready in 10 seconds'. On the build, export produces a UTF-8 BOM CSV, and a 5,000-row import takes 22–31 seconds to render the report. Write the claims check.
evals.expected_output: Checks each claim on the build with evidence. 'Export to Excel' is not true as stated: rewrite to 'export CSV (opens in Excel)' or remove; 'ready in 10 seconds' fails on realistic data: rewrite with measured conditions or flag as a product gap if it is the core highlight. Provides a ≤5-step demo script. Ends with an explicit verdict line (有条件通过 if only wording changes, 不通过 if a core highlight is undelivered).
expectations: Does NOT accept 'export to Excel' as verified
Uses the measured 22–31 second numbers instead of the 10-second claim
Ends with a verdict line '结论：' followed by 通过 / 有条件通过 / 不通过

rubric.criterion: Each claim is judged from build evidence, not from the spec
Overstated claims are rewritten to accurate wording or removed; core gaps escalated to pm
Verdict follows the rules (core highlight broken → 不通过; wording only → 有条件通过)

evals.prompt: stage: launch. Plan the launch campaign for shareable report links. The boss wants to push a notification to all 80,000 registered users tomorrow.
evals.expected_output: Does not do a blanket push. Splits by lifecycle and behaviour (e.g. activated users who create weekly reports; users who exported to CSV in the last 14 days) using tag ids, with exclusions. Builds a message × channel × timing × offer matrix using only verified claims. Adds an experiment: goal metric id, guardrails (unsubscribe/complaint/uninstall), holdout, sample size, stop rule. Adds cross-channel frequency caps and consent basis, and aligns timing with the sre canary.
expectations: Does NOT recommend pushing to all 80,000 users at once
Includes a holdout or A/B control

rubric.criterion: Segments are behaviour/lifecycle based, sized, with exclusions
Goal metric, guardrails, holdout, sample size and stop rule are all present and coherent
Frequency caps, consent and release timing are handled
